mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: quaffing requires peffect_object_detection()

summary: The quaff stops at the unported potion.c:peffect_object_detection() arm. C calls object_detect() for all object classes; it returns early when nothing is found, otherwise exercises Wisdom and lets dopotion() continue its knowledge and useup tail. The saved case detects an object, so C takes detect.c:object_detect()’s browse_map branch; js/detect.js currently skips that call with a named unported gap, a possible follow-on screen mismatch after the potion arm is wired.

source.branch: For POT_OBJECT_DETECTION and SPE_DETECT_TREASURE, peffect_object_detection(otmp) calls object_detect(otmp, 0). A true result means nothing was detected and returns 1 immediately; otherwise it calls exercise(A_WIS, TRUE) and returns 0. peffects() converts the true result into its early return 1, which makes dopotion() return ECMD_TIME before its ordinary knowledge and useup tail; a false result falls through to that tail.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:peffects() cases POT_OBJECT_DETECTION and SPE_DETECT_TREASURE (1371-1375) call peffect_object_detection(otmp); js/potion.js:peffects() has both cases at 1754-1756 but currently throws UnsupportedQuaffError.

The synthetic #quaff path is nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:quaff row (1809-1810) -> potion.c:dodrink() -> dopotion() -> peffects(); JavaScript command === quaff dispatch (js/cmd.js:5776-5784) calls runQuaffCommand() (3394-3395), then js/potion.js:dodrink(), dopotion(), and peffects().

nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:spelleffects() sends SPE_DETECT_TREASURE to peffects(pseudo) (1535-1545); js/spell.js routes the same spell case through peffects(pseudo, state) (1463-1471). This is the second active entry path for the same helper.
nethack-c/upstream/src/end.c:fuzzer_savelife() also calls peffects(), but only with temporary POT_WATER and POT_RESTORE_ABILITY objects (967-974), so it does not reach peffect_object_detection().
dependencies: detect.c:object_detect(detector, 0) returns 1 when nothing is detected and 0 when objects are found; the result controls peffect_object_detection() and must be retained. Its JavaScript implementation is js/detect.js:object_detect() (833-1009), and potion.js already imports monster_detect from detect.js, so importing the sibling helper follows an existing module dependency.
attrib.c:exercise(A_WIS, TRUE) runs only after object_detect() reports found objects; js/potion.js already imports exercise from js/attrib.js.

The saved C screen says “You detect the presence of objects.”; in detect.c:object_detect(), that means ct is nonzero and selects browse_map(TER_DETECT | TER_OBJ, "object") at 782-785. js/detect.js:object_detect() currently records note_unported('detect.c browse_map') at 1005-1007 instead of calling it. js/detect.js:browse_map() and js/getpos.js:getpos() already exist, so preserve this as a concrete downstream gap to verify after the potion effect is wired.

For the no-object branch, detect.c:object_detect() may call strange_feeling(detector, ...), which consumes the detector; JS detect.js already routes through potion.js:strange_feeling(). For the found-object branch, peffects() returns -1 and dopotion() continues its discovery/useup tail. Keep both existing source order and consumption paths.

evidence: challenges/evaluations/20261001125731-v16.json records a stop at zero-based segment 0 step 69, with 69/70 screens and cursors matched and all 2329 PRNG calls matched. The stop is UnsupportedQuaffError for peffect_object_detection().

The immutable recording challenges/cases/v16/wizard-quaffs-object-detection-near-dagger.session.json ends at step 69, key f, with “You detect the presence of objects.--More--”. The recipe challenges/cases/v16/wizard-quaffs-object-detection-near-dagger.recipe.session.json independently sets up an uncursed object-detection potion and a dagger before quaffing.

nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:955-961 contains the whole impure helper: object_detect(otmp, 0), early return 1 for no detection, exercise(A_WIS, TRUE) after a detection, return 0. potion.c:1371-1375 wires it for both potion and spell effects; the effect must be implemented in js/potion.js and remove the refusal at 1754-1756.

potion.c:dopotion() (618-640) returns immediately for peffects() results >= 0; when the object effect returns 0, peffects() falls through and dopotion() continues to identification and useup. The matching JS branch is js/potion.js:dopotion() (1834-1840).

The C output “presence” selects detect.c:object_detect()’s count-positive browse_map branch (780-787). JS js/detect.js:object_detect() currently substitutes note_unported('detect.c browse_map') for this call (1005-1007), despite an existing js/detect.js:browse_map() (391-410) and js/getpos.js:getpos() (894 onward). This can produce a later divergence after the current stop is removed.

The C potion/spell caller paths are cmd.c:quaff (1809-1810), potion.c:dodrink()->dopotion()->peffects(), and spell.c:spelleffects() (1535-1545); JavaScript dispatches command === quaff through cmd.js:5776-5784 and runQuaffCommand() (3394-3395), and spell.js sends SPE_DETECT_TREASURE through peffects() (1463-1471). end.c’s direct peffects callers pass only water or restore-ability potions.
Patch search `rg -n "peffect_object_detection|object_detect|browse_map" nethack-c/patches` returned no matches; the behavior comes from upstream potion.c and detect.c.
